- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot after spikes.
- Underestimate in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.15) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often holds high forecast for 2–3 days before adjusting.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating sustained upward trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising.
- Avoid averaging sentiment across all days — weight recent sentiment (last 3–5 days) more heavily for correction.
- If sentiment is flat or mildly negative, reduce forecast slope — model tends to assume continuation of trend even when sentiment weakens.
